claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you. That's a good start.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? By this I mean, are you the one providing for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and his general upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for all of his day-to-day care - his food, clothes, school things, everything he needs. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One more question:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances such as being in hospital, care, or living away from home for any extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a while now. He's been there for a couple of months or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. This is important information. I need to understand more about Alex's hospital stay:

**How many weeks exactly (or approximately) has Alex been in hospital?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

**During this 11-week hospital stay, have you been regularly spending money on Alex - for example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have been spending money on him while he's been in hospital. I still buy him clothes, magazines, and his favorite snacks and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News!

Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
✓ You live in the UK
✓ You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care
✓ Alex lives with you (when not in hospital)
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Regarding Alex's hospital stay:**

Although Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is still within the 12-week limit before Child Benefit would normally be affected. More importantly, because you are regularly spending money on Alex (buying him clothes, magazines, snacks, etc.), you would qualify to continue receiving Child Benefit even if his hospital stay extends beyond 12 weeks.

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can do so through the government's Child Benefit application process. If his hospital stay does extend longer, make sure to inform HMRC about your situation and the fact that you're regularly spending money on him, as this ensures your payments can continue.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
